strengths: Clear and well-motivated insight unifying denoising across generative model paradigms
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 diverse generative models with extensive ablations
Strong empirical results achieving state-of-the-art for MAR models without semantics distillation (FID 1.35 for MAR-L)
Excellent generalization: works across AR/non-AR models, multiple architectures (ViT/CNN), and tokenizer topologies (2D/1D/VQ)
Important practical finding that semantics-distilled tokenizers fail to generalize to AR models while l-DeTok does
Independence from external pretrained models makes it applicable to domains like video and audio
Thorough reproducibility with extensive implementation details, promised code, and training cost analysis
Addresses practical issues (grokking phenomenon in 1D tokenizers) with concrete solutions
weaknesses: Limited theoretical understanding of why denoising helps; core design choices (interpolative noise, noise schedules) lack principled justification

Training-inference discrepancy: decoder trained on corrupted latents but operates on clean embeddings; requires 100-epoch fine-tuning to recover performance, suggesting gains may primarily come from encoder regularization rather than the denoising objective itself
Moderate experimental scale (O(10^6) samples) with no evidence of scaling to web-scale; acknowledged as open question
Limited technical novelty: applies well-established denoising autoencoders and masking (MAE) to tokenizers; incremental contribution
Incomplete analysis: latent noise alone nearly achieves joint results for non-AR models (5.56 vs 5.50 FID), yet masking is included without clear justification
No error bars or variance estimates; CFG scale selection 'searched from FID@10k' could overfit to this metric
Multiple design choices appear ad-hoc: masking ratio bias (Eq. 5), GAN loss timing at epoch 100, noise schedule variations showing similar results
Mechanism of spot artifact removal in text-to-image generation unexplained
